why: B (Cartan–Hadamard): on every abstract connected Hausdorff ℝⁿ-manifold with any smooth Mathlib RiemannianBundle metric and any Levi-Civita connection, Milnor-complete, simply connected (Mathlib SimplyConnectedSpace) with ⟨R(A,B)A,B⟩ ≤ 0: any p, q are joined by a geodesic [0,1] → M unique on [0,1], and M is diffeomorphic to ℝⁿ (Mathlib Diffeomorph). A (universes 0): for slice submanifolds N ⊆ V with the induced metric only: closed ⇒ complete; a covering exp_p of a simply connected N is injective; exp_p onto for complete connected N; and Theorem 19.2 (unique unbroken geodesic in Ω(N; p, q), N ≅ ℝ^{dim N} as Mathlib Diffeomorph). A ⇒ B fails genuinely (abstract manifolds are not given embedded; no Nash embedding, no abstract exp/covering theory); B ⇒ A fails genuinely (setting; A's auxiliary statements about closed N and coverings are not consequences of B). On embedded manifolds A ⇒ B_emb and B_emb ⇒ Theorem 19.2 (model ℝⁿ) are both proved. B is fine for n = 0, 1.
overlap: No A_to_B/B_to_A. For the embedded theorem B_emb_to_A_cplt: 498 shared project theorems — Hopf–Rinow (theorem_10_9, isGeodesicallyComplete_of_isRiemComplete, riemDist lemmas, normal coordinates) and the geodesic-flow infrastructure, used only by the completeness dictionary Emb.metricComplete_of_complete; curvature (curvOp_mem, curvR_of_mem), slice-chart and tangent-projection lemmas from the Bridge. Not shared: the covering-map argument (isCoveringMap_expToN, injective_expToN_of_simplyConnected, isLocalDiffeomorph_expToN, expDiffeomorph, lemma_19_1, theorem_18_1).
